Illustrative driver profiles

Driver profiles show readiness, assigned work, and the reason a record needs attention.

These demo records are illustrative only. They show how BOF can present a driver profile without exposing real driver private data: readiness state, home base, assigned load, document status, DQF score, and next action stay visible for operations review.

Drivers + BOF Vault

Driver documents become readiness signals before dispatch depends on them.

BOF Vault belongs inside the driver workflow as the intake mechanism for CDL, medical card, MVR, DQF, policy acknowledgements, renewal-risk records, and HR handoff context. BOF then turns those documents into practical readiness signals for dispatch, safety, settlement, and business-office follow-through.

Fleet-owned driver files

Each driver record has the paperwork a fleet owner expects to inspect.

BOF separates the fleet's own driver qualification files from outside carrier packet records. A carrier can be attached to the load, but BOF does not pretend the fleet owner controls another company's employee file.

Document groupRequired driver recordsCurrent proof for DRV-2048Release effect
Identity and licenseCDL, driver license image, license class, expiration, endorsementsCurrentDriver can stay assigned to TMS-LD-10482.
Medical and safetyMedical card, MCSA exam summary, MVR, clearinghouse, drug and alcohol policy acknowledgementCurrentNo safety blocker on the selected load.
Employment fileEmployment application, resume or work history, prior employer inquiry, road test certificate, annual reviewFiledSupports dispatch eligibility.
Emergency and contactEmergency contact, phone/email, home terminal, driver communication acknowledgementFiledBack office knows who to contact during exception follow-up.
Tax and settlementW-9 or I-9 status, payment preference, bank/settlement setup, owner-operator packet if applicableProtected and filedSensitive details stay out of the public review while settlement readiness remains visible.
Dispatch controlsELD/mobile acknowledgement, route notes, load assignment, safety hold status, dispatch eligibility noteEligibleDriver file does not block release.

Safe Demo Data Rule

Public examples use synthetic labels, initials, and status summaries instead of full private driver records.

Allowed

Not shown

Why it matters
The page demonstrates operating readiness without implying live customer data exposure

Who uses this

Dispatch, safety, and operations leads use the same eligibility answer instead of reconciling separate driver files.

Next action

Release ready drivers, keep watch drivers in review, and resolve credential holds before assignment.

Driver system access controls

Driver readiness includes how records are accessed and submitted.

Driver portal access, mobile uploads, ELD-related records, and acknowledgements are governed by written IT and data protection controls.

Acceptable use

Driver and back-office users operate inside clear expectations for system use, record handling, and responsible access.

DAT-IT-001

Password and authentication

Credential records and driver-system access are supported by authentication requirements and access discipline.

DAT-IT-007

Mobile Device and ELD

Driver uploads, ELD-related records, and mobile document capture have a written security basis.

DAT-IT-006

Remote access and communications

Remote follow-up, driver messaging, and back-office communications stay tied to controlled access expectations.
